about:
Amsted Automotive, headquartered in Saginaw, Michigan, was formed in 2021 through the integration of Burgess-Norton (established 1903) and Means Industries (established 1922), along with Transform Automotive (1997) and SMW Manufacturing (2004). The combined entity operates 21 facilities across North America, Europe, and Asia.

The company designs and manufactures high-performance components for vehicle and industrial applications, including brackets, welded assemblies, coupler components, piston pins, bearing products, wear parts, and powertrain components. Core processes include cold forming, powder metallurgy, advanced metal forming (flow forming, in-die spline forming, grob forming, laser welding, stamping), and propulsion systems (torque management, clutch technologies). With over 2,000 employees across 21 facilities worldwide (13 in the U.S.), Amsted produces more than 200 million components annually.

Amsted serves global automotive, off-highway, mining, and industrial markets. Its components are used in electric heavy-duty e-axles, wheel-end bolts and hubs, traditional and hybrid powertrains, brake systems, electric drivelines, chassis and suspension systems, fluid conveyance, and industrial cutting tools. Customers include automakers and Tier 1 suppliers seeking flexible manufacturing across internal combustion, hybrid, and electric propulsion architectures.

The company emphasizes its regional manufacturing footprint—13 U.S. facilities plus global sites—to mitigate tariff risks and supply delays, enabling production close to customer demand. Its integration of legacy brands brings together cold forming, powder metallurgy, and advanced metal forming expertise to deliver tailored, high-quality components for evolving propulsion technologies.
